purpose: Fillable formatting outline; team-written content and official cover required

blocks.text: Report Working Template

TEAM CONTENT REQUIRED. This is a formatting scaffold, not a completed academic submission. Keep the official cover fields accurate. Supply your own problem argument, related-work evaluation, interpretation and actual contributions. Resolve permitted AI use with the tutor before submitting generated material.

The assignment requests around 40 pages and fewer than 50. These page allocations are planning aids, not permission to pad a report with blank pages. This scaffold is intentionally shorter and cannot pass final report readiness while team content is missing.
Introduction and problem statement

[TEAM: State the team's research question, warehouse assumptions and practical limits. Evaluate the need using sources you have read; identify what is distinctive without claiming unverified novelty.]
Related systems and literature
[TEAM: Compare the systems and primary papers the team actually reviewed. Explain which assumptions and conclusions apply to this partially observed simulation, and which do not.]
Environment and state preparation
[TEAM: Explain map construction, public sensing/memory, actions, rewards and ending rules. Trace a real observation and distinguish robot knowledge from viewer truth.]
Algorithms and implementation

[TEAM: Each member explains their actual code contribution. Describe Q-learning, SARSA, DQN, PPO and the separately labeled ensemble using the implemented versions, not textbook guarantees that do not apply.]
Experimental design and optimization

[TEAM: Describe registered candidates, actual budgets, seeds, checkpoints, development selection and the once-used product holdout. Keep the later ensemble study development-only. Justify settings using your own analysis.]
Results and visualization

[TEAM: Insert verified figures/tables and explain denominators. Discuss official returns, steps, Waits, failures and timing. Do not compare different populations as a before/after effect or claim universal reliability.]
Discussion limitations and contributions

[TEAM: Write the team's interpretation and compare it with the reviewed literature. Explain partial-observation failures, one-seed limitations, ensemble cost and actual individual work. Attach evidence of completed contributions.]
Conclusion
[TEAM: Answer your research question using the measured scope. State unresolved weaknesses and distinguish completed work from future work.]
References
[TEAM: Use the required citation style and only sources you actually consulted. Confirm metadata; cite libraries/code and AI assistance where required.]
Submission checks

[TEAM: Provide the real member list/IDs, completed individual contribution evidence and project plan, tutor-approved scope, final report review, completed separate rubric and prescribed AI Usage Disclosure Form. Rehearse explanations and a code modification; do not invent sign-offs or contributions.]
